Subject: Grade boundary mapping & hiring velocity impact — proposal

Team — attaching the first-pass grade boundary mapping and a brief note on how band widths affect our ability to move candidates through offers (hiring velocity). High-level asks below.

Attachment: grade_mapping_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet: proposed grade bands, midpoint ranges, suggested geo modifiers)

Why this now:
- We need a clearer mapping between leveling (grade boundaries) and practical offer ranges so recruiters and hiring managers can make quick decisions without repeated approvals.
- Recent offer cycles for mid-SWE roles showed variance across US regions; we think band width is a driver of time-to-offer when managers request escalations.

Proposed decisions to surface in this thread:
1) Whether to tighten band widths for grades E3–E5 for US and EU to reduce negotiation windows.
2) Whether to adopt a three-tier geo modifier (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3) with fixed percentage deltas instead of freehand adjustments.
3) Pilot plan: apply to next 10 active reqs and measure days-to-offer and accepted offer delta.

Please review the spreadsheet and reply with:
- Quick thumbs (agree / disagree) on the three items above
- Any major pushback on the numeric midpoints and percentiles (sheet tab: market-metrics)
- Recommended pilot cohort (suggest IDs or functions) by EOD Friday 2026-09-24.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Grade boundary mapping & hiring velocity impact — proposal

Thanks Karthik — quick notes after a pass on the draft. Attaching a PDF with inline comments.

Attachment: neha_comments.pdf (PDF: annotated comments on grade_mapping_draft.xlsx)

Summary of my top-level feedback:
- Agree with tightening E3–E5 in US core markets (SF/NY/SEA) — narrower bands reduce negotiation windows.
- For EU, prefer to keep slightly wider bands for localized flexibility given multiple currencies and strong local market variance.
- Tiered geo modifier is clean and easier to operationalize; suggest Tier 1 = +0%, Tier 2 = -6%, Tier 3 = -12% relative to national midpoint rather than absolute deltas. This preserves internal parity.
- Pilot cohort: recommend focusing on Product (3 reqs), Mid-SWE (4 reqs), and Sales AE (3 reqs) — total 10. Exclude senior IC and leadership for this pilot.

Open question: how do we treat relocation offers vs local hires within the tiers? I suggest a short addendum clarifying that temporary relocation packages are additive and not reflected in the band.

On the data side: Mercer sent a short supplement on LATAM variance; should we bring them into a 30-min sync to validate the Tier breakpoints?

-Neha
Head of Compensation Programs
Redwood Inference

Copying the thread for a quick note from ops perspective.

I support tightening E3–E5 for core US markets but want to flag two operational impacts:
- Manager escalations will spike the week we announce changes unless we automate an FAQ + one-click escalation flow in Greenhouse. Recommend we pre-build the escalation template and the “manager quick-approve” checkbox.
- For LATAM and APAC pockets, my preference is to keep a slightly broader operational band and then map to local allowances (housing/bench stipends). Narrow bands in those regions may cause repeated exceptions and slow down hiring velocity rather than speed it up.

Proposal for pilot measurement: measure days-to-offer and % of offers requiring comp escalation for a 30-day window post-implementation; report back with a short dashboard (two slides). If the pilot shows >15% escalation uplift, we revert.

If we agree on the Tier definitions (Neha’s suggestion), I can have People Ops build the escalation template and schedule a 30-min rollout sync with recruiting next Monday.

-Marissa
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick recap and next steps below.

Decisions made in-thread:
- Tighten E3–E5 band widths for US Tier 1 markets as discussed.
- Adopt Neha’s three-tier geo modifier suggestion (Tier 1 = +0%, Tier 2 = -6%, Tier 3 = -12%).
- For EU, maintain slightly wider bands but freeze any manual country-level deltas until we validate Mercer’s LATAM/EU supplement.
- Pilot cohort approved: Product (3), Mid-SWE (4), Sales AE (3). Pilot start: 2026-10-04. Measurement window: 30 days.

Action items: 
- Marissa: build the Greenhouse escalation template + manager quick-approve checkbox (due 2026-10-01).
- Neha: schedule 30-min sync with Mercer (benchmarks@mercer.com) to validate Tier breakpoints and share the Mercer supplement (due 2026-09-30).
- Laura: confirm communication cadence for managers and a short FAQ doc (due 2026-09-29).
- Karthik: update the master spreadsheet and post v2 to Drive (done). Attachment: grade_mapping_v2.xlsx

Meeting: I scheduled a 30-min pilot kickoff with Recruiting on 2026-10-04 09:00 PT. Calendar invite sent.

Closing note: keep exceptions documented in HR-7482 (we’ll use the ticket to track any reverts).

-Karthik
